chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hakam narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Samt al-Bajali, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): What do you say about the weakened ones?

He said to me, as if terrified: And have you left anyone to be (in a state of being) weakened? And where are the weakened ones? For by Allah, your matter has been carried by shoulders to shoulders in their houses and it has been spoken of by rumor collectors in the roads of Medina.

key_terms.السَّقَايَاتُ: Rumor collectors or those who spread news
key_terms.الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ: The weakened ones (those lacking power or strength)

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam say about the state of weakness among the Muslims?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to highlight the Imam’s rhetorical shock that the community has normalized a state of 'weakness' (istid'af), where their affairs are no longer guarded but openly discussed by women in their homes and servants in the streets. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the transition from the era of political and social vulnerability to the expectation of divine support, warning against the complacency that allows public affairs to become common knowledge among the general populace.
